blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) often underperforms full fine-tuning, especially in heterogeneous and continual-learning settings in which substantial forgetting occurs. In general, it suffers from an undesirable learning-forgetting trade-off across diverse fine-tuning settings. We identify a potential contributor: LoRA adapters, especially high-rank ones, frequently fail to realize the available capacity afforded by the configured rank. Specifically, we find that standard LoRA updates have effective rank far below their configured rank, limiting how broadly the update energy is distributed. Therefore, we propose training mechanisms that optimize the original objective while maximizing adapter effective rank. Our main method adds a simple, stable, differentiable, and SVD-free Rényi-2 effective-rank regularizer to the language-modeling loss. We also connect capacity maximization to norm-bounded updates. In mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models evaluated with multiple random seeds, a penalty weight of $λ=0.01$ lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least $16$ relative to unpenalized LoRA. Mean training perplexity improves or increases by at most $0.02$ in all but one model-rank comparison. Single-task and scheduling experiments further show that the balance between learning and retention depends on the configuration. We also observe that several LoRA variants in the literature also suffer from the identified capacity issue, and our approach provides a complementary axis of improvement to LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These results suggest that effective rank is not only a post-hoc diagnostic of adapter quality, but a trainable objective for improving the learning-forgetting frontier. Our code is available at https://github.com/tomohiro-sawada/lora-capacity-utilization

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Low-rank adaptation (LoRA; Hu et al., 2022 ) is a standard parameter-efficient alternative to full fine-tuning: it scales to large models, is easy to compose with existing training stacks, and is widely treated as the default way to specialize a pretrained language model on a new task or domain Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) ; Biderman et al. (2024) .
A common piece of practitioner wisdom is that increasing LoRA rank increases adapter capacity: a larger r r enlarges the low-rank update subspace and can support richer task-specific changes Raschka (2023) ; Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) ; Liu et al. (2024b) .
This intuition is appealing and often borne out at moderate ranks, yet it rests on an implicit assumption that is rarely checked: that the adapter actually uses the subspace it is given.
blocks.zh:
低等级的适应(LORA;Hu等人,2022年)是完全微调后的一种标准参数高效的替代方案:它缩放到大模型上,容易与现有的训练堆叠组成,被广泛视为默认的方法,将预训语言模型专门用于新任务或域名Schulman和思维机器实验室(2025年);Biderman等人(2024年).
一个常见的从业者智慧是,提高LORA的排名会提高适配器容量:一个更大的r 扩大了低级更新子空间,可以支持更丰富的任务特定变化 Raschka (2023); Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025); Liu等人 (2024b) .
这种直觉是有吸引力的,而且往往在中位得到证实,然而它基于一种隐含的假设,这种假设很少被检查:适配器实际使用它得到的子空间.

blocks.en:
In parallel, fine-tuning, whether full-rank or parameter-efficient, faces a persistent learning–forgetting tension.
Fitting a target distribution can improve task metrics while erasing competence on broad pretraining domains, and heterogeneous or sequential training regimes exacerbate the trade-off Kirkpatrick et al. (2017) ; Hu et al. (2022) .
LoRA is not exempt: in mixed-domain and continual-learning settings, adapters often lag full fine-tuning on target-task fit while still paying a substantial retention cost on pretraining proxies Biderman et al. (2024) ; Shuttleworth et al. (2024) .
Prior work has proposed many remedies, such as
stronger parameterizations Kopiczko et al. (2024) , norm constraints Wang et al. (2025) , spectral initialization Meng et al. (2025) , and deliberately tiny adapters Morris et al. (2026) . However, these approaches frequently reallocate the trade-off rather than improve it: methods that fit the fine-tuning mixture well can forget aggressively, whereas methods that limit forgetting often underfit the new data (Figure 2 ).

LORA并非例外:在混合领域和持续学习的环境下,适配器常常在目标任务配置上落后于全面微调,同时仍然为Biderman等人(2024年)的预训代理人支付大量保留费用; Shuttleworth等人(2024年).

blocks.en:
We argue that a useful missing variable in this picture is not nominal configured rank r r but the actual realized adapter capacity that we measure in terms of effective rank .
Let Δ ​ W \Delta W denote the accumulated LoRA update on a target layer.
Following Roy and Vetterli (2007) , we measure how many directions effectively carry singular-value mass using the effective rank erank ⁡ ( Δ ​ W ) \mathrm{erank}(\Delta W) , a continuous relaxation of matrix rank obtained from the entropy of the normalized spectrum.
Intuitively, erank ⁡ ( Δ ​ W ) \mathrm{erank}(\Delta W) reports how uniformly the update distributes its singular-value mass across its singular directions: a highly skewed spectrum behaves like a low-rank update in practice even when r r is large.
Across three fine-tuning settings, standard LoRA training underutilizes capacity in exactly this sense: we observe in Figure 1 that the utilization quotient erank ⁡ ( Δ ​ W ) / r \mathrm{erank}(\Delta W)/r tends to be much smaller than 1.0 1.0 and even more strikingly, it falls as configured rank grows (Section 2 ).
The key observation is therefore that configured rank is an unreliable proxy for usable capacity : scaling r r alone does not reliably deliver “more adapter” in the sense that matters for learning and retention.

blocks.en:
This distinction matters because the learning–forgetting trade-off is not only about how large an update is, but about how that update is distributed across the orthogonal directions of the weight.
Spectral analyses of finetuned weights in prior work emphasize that adaptation can introduce directions weakly aligned with the pretrained spectrum (so-called intruder dimensions ), and that the prevalence and weighting of such directions correlate with forgetting Shuttleworth et al. (2024) .
However, in our analysis (§ 5 ), every method that fits the mixture well, dense fine-tuning included, places most of its singular-value mass on such directions; only the methods that underfit (VeRA, TinyLoRA, SVF) avoid them.
Therefore, we argue that the relevant question is not whether intruder dimensions exist, but whether the dominant part of the update uses the allocated rank budget in a balanced, information-bearing way.
We therefore ask: can we improve the learning–forgetting frontier by maximizing realized capacity during training? Since erank ⁡ ( Δ ​ W ) ≤ r \mathrm{erank}(\Delta W)\leq r Roy and Vetterli (2007) , increasing utilization means driving the normalized spectrum toward uniformity subject to the task loss.

blocks.en:
Concretely, we study regularized training objectives that augment the standard language-modeling loss L L with a capacity regularization term that focuses on maximizing the effective rank.
Direct spectral differentiation requires care at rank-deficient updates and incurs SVD overhead (Appendix D .1). We therefore use an SVD-free surrogate, the Rényi-2 effective rank erank 2 ​ ( Δ ​ W ) \mathrm{erank}_{2}(\Delta W) . We develop two approaches to increasing this effective-rank surrogate.
First, norm-bounded capacity maximization couples a Roy–Vetterli lower bound with Norm-Bounded LoRA (NB-LoRA) Wang et al. (2025) : by enforcing an operator-norm cap and maximizing the Frobenius norm within that cap, one can raise effective rank through a principled constrained reparameterization.
This strategy works in practice but limits the adapter weight updates to a specialized parameterization which often results in unstable training empirically.
Therefore, we propose a simpler, differentiable, parameterization-agnostic and easy-to-optimize regularization strategy called the Rényi-2 penalty as our main method, which directly maximizes erank 2 ​ ( Δ ​ W ) \mathrm{erank}_{2}(\Delta W) .
This penalty is not only applicable to vanilla LoRA, but also to improved spectral variants such as PiSSA Meng et al. (2025) and LoRA-XS Bałazy et al. (2025) .

blocks.en: In summary, our core contributions are: i) we identify systematic capacity underutilization in standard LoRA training, especially at high configured rank, and argue that realized effective rank, not nominal rank, is the relevant unit of analysis for adapter capacity, ii) we formulate effective-rank maximization as a principled objective atop standard language-modeling loss, with both a norm-bounded reparameterization route (NB-LoRA) and a parameterization-agnostic surrogate, iii) we introduce the Rényi-2 penalty , a unitary-invariant, SVD-free effective-rank regularizer that is simple to implement and stable to optimize, and demonstrate improvements in the learning–forgetting trade-off across mixed-domain and single-task fine-tuning settings, and iv) we provide spectral diagnostics (intruder mass, soft global coupling) that provide a novel lens to characterize the relationship between singular directions of updated weights and the pretrained weights.

blocks.en: 4.2 Effectiveness of Norm-bounded Instantiation
blocks.zh: 4.2 规范性证据的有效性

blocks.en: While most of the paper is focused on our Rényi-2 penalty approach, in this section we observe that our other instantiation based on norm-bounded LoRA (§ 3.2 ), although a little unstable, also performs reasonably well. Table 1 compares NB-LoRA, with and without the Frobenius-norm capacity term in Equation ( 4 ), against standard LoRA and dense down-projection fine-tuning. We observe that simply bounding the norm raises erank \mathrm{erank} ( 504 504 vs. 341 341 ) and lowers Wiki perplexity ( 20.1 20.1 vs. 21.1 21.1 ). Increasing λ \lambda raises effective rank further and lowers Wiki perplexity to 19.1 19.1 . Train PPL ( 23.7 23.7 – 24.3 24.3 ) and StarCoder PPL ( 4.02 4.02 – 4.11 4.11 ) are slightly worse than standard LoRA’s ( 22.6 22.6 and 4.00 4.00 ), and the training fit is worse than dense down-projection fine-tuning’s ( 21.0 21.0 ). blocks.en: 4.3 Rényi-2 penalty on LoRA variants
blocks.zh: 4.3 对LORA变体的Rényi-2处罚

blocks.en: Since our approach is readily applicable to LoRA variants (§ 3 ), we apply the Rényi-2 penalty to PiSSA and LoRA-XS – the two variants with the highest Wiki perplexity in Figure 2 . Table 2 shows that the penalty improves their results on single-task GSM8K adaptation.

blocks.en:
At λ = 0 \lambda{=}0 , PiSSA already attains large erank \mathrm{erank} ( 829 829 , near dense down-projection fine-tuning’s 839 839 ) but severe Wiki forgetting.
Increasing λ \lambda monotonically raises erank \mathrm{erank} to 896 896 and reduces Wiki and StarCoder perplexity by 3.5 3.5 and 0.4 0.4 points, respectively, while slightly improving GSM8K Train PPL. The penalty therefore reshapes how an already high-rank PiSSA update uses its degrees of freedom, rather than merely increasing nominal rank.

blocks.en:
LoRA-XS without penalty also demonstrates severe forgetting with a moderate erank = 565 \mathrm{erank}=565 .
Our regularizer increases erank \mathrm{erank} by approximately 330 330 to 895 895 and cuts Wiki perplexity by 5.4 5.4 points at λ = 1 \lambda{=}1 , with the best Train PPL in the sweep.
This is direct evidence that subspace-constrained adapters can leave capacity on the table, and that maximizing the Rényi-2 effective-rank surrogate can reduce this underutilization.

blocks.en:

Two mechanisms may help explain the training–retention trade-off.
First, linear mode connectivity ( Frankle et al., 2020 ) : after a sufficient number of steps, the model may enter a basin of the language-modeling loss in which the solution is comparatively robust to perturbations.
Applying the penalty in that late phase reshapes the adapter spectrum without derailing Hausa fit.
Activating it from the outset interferes with the initial trajectory into that basin and inflates Train PPL even when forgetting is minimized.

blocks.en: Three qualitative regimes emerge. First, VeRA and TinyLoRA exhibit near-saturated coupling to the pretrained spectrum: weighted unaligned mass is near zero, and the unaligned count is also small (especially for VeRA), with small H soft H_{\mathrm{soft}} . Second, a broad LoRA-like band—including Standard LoRA, Rényi-2 penalty, PiSSA, LoRA-XS, and (to a slightly lesser extent) dense down-projection fine-tuning—leaves ≳ 96 % \gtrsim 96\% of directions unaligned at this strict threshold. In this regime, count-based comparisons are nearly flat, but where the spectral mass lands still differs: LoRA-XS places the largest fraction of spectral weight on directions without a strong pretrained partner, consistent with its adaptation being carried by dominant singular directions that are more decoupled from pretraining. Third, SVF with an intermediate H soft H_{\mathrm{soft}} illustrates that count and mass can decouple sharply: it has near-zero weighted unaligned mass but a much lower unaligned rate than the LoRA-like band, indicating that SVF concentrates most of the finetuned matrix’s singular-value mass on a small set of strongly pretrained-like directions while leaving a long tail of low-weight directions without strong partners.

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en:
Roy and Vetterli (2007) ’s effective rank summarizes how uniformly singular-value mass is distributed; we build on their definition and on Rényi entropies Rényi (1961) ; Cover and Thomas (2006) to obtain a unitary-invariant surrogate ( erank 2 \mathrm{erank}_{2} ) suitable for gradient-based training.
To our knowledge, prior PEFT work has not targeted maximizing realized adapter rank during language-model fine-tuning as a means to improve the learning–forgetting frontier; rank-stabilized scaling Kalajdzievski (2023) and spectral initializations Meng et al. (2025) ; Wang et al. (2024) address adjacent but distinct failure modes.

据我们所知,先前的PEFT工作没有在语言模型微调时针对最大化已实现的适配器等级,作为改进学习的手段——忘记边疆;等级稳定缩放Kalajdzievski(2023年)和光谱初始化Meng等人(2025年);Wang等人。 (2024)解决相邻但截然不同的失败模式.

blocks.en:
A large body of prior work studies how to configure LoRA—rank and scaling Raschka (2023) ; Kalajdzievski (2023) , which modules to target Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) , and whether LoRA can match full fine-tuning in post-training regimes Schulman and Thinking Machines Lab (2025) ; Biderman et al. (2024) .
These works largely treat configured rank r r or trainable parameter count as mere hyperparameters.
Orthogonal to utilization, PEFT methods also differ in their trainable budget and in how the update is tied to the pretrained spectrum.
VeRA Kopiczko et al. (2024) , Singular Value fine-tuning Sun et al. (2022) , and TinyLoRA Morris et al. (2026) restrict trainable degrees of freedom by several orders of magnitude.
LoRA-XS Bałazy et al. (2025) also reduces the budget, training only an r × r r\times r core inside a frozen truncated-SVD subspace ( 1.9 × 10 7 1.9\times 10^{7} versus 1.2 × 10 8 1.2\times 10^{8} parameters at r = 896 r{=}896 in our setup), yet still admits a rank- r r update.
PiSSA Meng et al. (2025) keeps LoRA’s budget and instead changes the initialization to the principal singular directions of the pretrained weight.
We benchmark against all three regimes in Section 4.1 ; our penalty is complementary in that it improves utilization within a fixed parameterization rather than reallocating the budget itself.

blocks.en:
Fine-tuning improves target-task metrics but can erase competence on broad pretraining domains, and heterogeneous or sequential training amplifies the tension Kirkpatrick et al. (2017) . Biderman et al. (2024) systematically compare LoRA and full fine-tuning, showing that low-rank adapters typically learn less on the target domain but also forget less off it, and that full fine-tuning’s effective update rank can exceed typical LoRA configurations by an order of magnitude.
Norm- and magnitude-aware variants such as DoRA Liu et al. (2024a) , DeLoRA Bini et al. (2025) , and Norm-Bounded LoRA Wang et al. (2025) pursue a related goal—making directional updates behave more like full fine-tuning Aghajanyan et al. (2020) —but through reparameterization rather than explicit control of spectral utilization.
Continued-pretraining methods such as ReLoRA Lialin et al. (2023) accumulate high-rank structure by merging and restarting low-rank updates over long horizons; we instead ask how to use a single adapter’s rank budget more fully during standard SFT.

blocks.en:
A growing line of work engineers fine-tuning through the singular structure of weight matrices.
PiSSA Meng et al. (2025) initializes adapters from dominant singular components; MiLoRA Wang et al. (2024) instead adapts minor components to reduce interference with pretrained knowledge; AdaLoRA Zhang et al. (2023) adaptively reallocates rank across modules; and SVF Sun et al. (2022) trains singular values directly.
These methods change which subspace or spectrum is updated, often at the cost of an explicit or implicit SVD.
Our Rényi-2 penalty is orthogonal and complementary to these approaches.

这些方法改变了哪个子空间或频谱被更新,往往以明示或暗示的SVD为代价.
我们的Rényi-2惩罚是正统的,是对这些做法的补充。

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
Standard LoRA training often underutilizes its allocated subspace
so nominal rank is an unreliable proxy for usable adapter capacity in the learning–forgetting trade-off.
We proposed effective-rank maximization via the Rényi-2 penalty, a parameterization-agnostic, SVD-free term added to the language-modeling loss, and showed across mixed-domain SFT, task-specific SFT, rank sweeps, and scheduling ablations that it can reduce forgetting on pretraining proxies while maintaining competitive target-task fit.
In mixed-domain rank sweeps on three models, λ = 0.01 \lambda=0.01 lowers mean Wiki perplexity at every tested rank of at least 16 16 relative to unpenalized LoRA, with mean Train PPL improving
or increasing by at most 0.02 0.02 in all but one comparison.
Our single-task and scheduling experiments also demonstrate
configuration-dependent learning and retention outcomes:
the penalty can improve retention without a large training-fit
cost, but does not eliminate the learning–forgetting trade-off.
Spectral diagnostics provide descriptive comparisons of the resulting updates.
Effective rank is therefore not merely a post-hoc diagnostic but a trainable objective that regularizes toward fuller utilization.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: While capacity maximization improves the learning–forgetting frontier in several configurations, benefits depend on the metric and execution, and the method still requires task-specific tuning of λ \lambda and may not be beneficial when the goal is deliberate underfitting or strong retention of a very narrow domain. The present study focuses on LoRA-style adapters and closely related spectral variants; extending the same objective to other PEFT families or to full fine-tuning may require different regularization schedules or parameterizations.

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: The paper studies general-purpose language-model adaptation on public benchmark data and does not introduce new user data collection. The main ethical risk is indirect: methods that improve adaptation efficiency can be repurposed to more rapidly specialize models for harmful or deceptive uses. We therefore frame the contribution as an optimization and analysis tool, not as a deployment recommendation, and recommend the usual safeguards for downstream release, including dataset provenance checks, benchmark leakage review, and task-appropriate human oversight.
blocks.zh: 论文研究了公共基准数据的通用语言模型适应性,没有引入新的用户数据收集. 主要的道德风险是间接的:提高适应效率的方法可以重新用于更快速的专业化模式,用于有害或欺骗性用途。 因此,我们将该贡献确定为优化和分析工具,而不是部署建议,并建议下游释放的通常保障措施,包括数据集出处检查、基准渗漏审查和适合任务的人力监督。

The exact capacity term is therefore constant over nonzero rank-one updates and supplies no preference among them. This is an algebraic boundary case; we report no rank-one experiment. Numerical stabilization near the zero update is separate from this statement about the exact objective.
